title: Any second now
logline: A local TV crew at dusk interviews a man in his farmyard about the UFO he says comes over his barn every night. They give up and walk away; behind their backs, with their camera still rolling at the hip, it comes.
times: playback seconds of the 30.00 s take. Slow motion runs 24.0-26.3 s (30 % speed, back to full speed by 26.7 s); no line is spoken inside it.
rate: every line at 2.5-2.8 words per second

lines.speaker: Farmer
lines.text: Every night at ten, it comes right over that barn.
lines.delivery: Plain and certain, a man stating a fact he is tired of defending.
lines.gesture: On "over that barn" he twists to his right and points his right arm fully straight back over his shoulder at the barn roof.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.delivery: Bright TV voice, a little patient, as if humouring him.
lines.gesture: She has just thrust the mic in under his chin with her right arm.

lines.speaker: Farmer
lines.delivery: Quiet, sure, glancing up from his watch.
lines.gesture: Left wrist raised to his face, reading his watch; lowers it as he finishes.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Okay... I think we've got enough.
lines.delivery: Polite, already finished with him; the pause after "Okay" says it.
lines.gesture: Lowers the mic, a small open left hand, then turns toward the van.

lines.speaker: Farmer
lines.delivery: A shout, the moment speed returns to normal.
lines.gesture: Right arm fully up, pointing at the saucer as it streaks away.

lines.speaker: Farmer
lines.delivery: Out of breath, half hope, half dread; not a shout.
lines.gesture: Turned to the crew, his right arm still raised to the empty sky, sinking slowly to his side.
